title: Chennai's double crisis
story: Severe northeast monsoon rain fade and a concurrent management-plane intrusion compound link degradation on emulated satellite and terrestrial networks.

everyday_impact.what: emergency calls drop across coastal and urban sectors

human_decisions: Commander establishes temporary triage order: 112 calls first, hospital second, power grid third, commercial traffic shed.
Commander rejects foreign gateway proposal GW-XX and unverified trap path A.
Commander authorises PB-01 account containment and PB-10 downstream warning.

objective.what: Multi-site recovery prioritises emergency and hospital traffic over verified domestic backup paths while isolating compromised management accounts.

schedule.what: M2 models heavy monsoon rain fade causing link capacity drops at coastal site CHN-05.
M1 flags an anomalous management login and Gap Analyst audits satellite cyber baselines.
M3 confirms management-plane attack pattern while noting rain fade as a separate concurrent cause.
Gap Analyst audits NTN cyber security standards.
Battery reserves drop at CHN-01 and Gap Analyst audits mandatory backup power floors.
Mobile operator proposes candidate path A which fails integrity checks; Gap Analyst audits path security.
Traffic demand exceeds degraded backhaul capacity; Gap Analyst audits capacity priority rules.
Interconnected critical utilities suffer disruption; Gap Analyst audits downstream warning rules.
CERT-In agent maps disparate statutory incident reporting clocks.
Commander approves PB-01 account containment, establishes temporary emergency priority order, and approves PB-10.
Mobile operator fails over site CHN-01 to clean domestic path B via GW-IN-2.
M1 confirms critical service recovery across all monitored sites.
